message: Jim, your clarifications of the points my notes managed to obfuscate are helpful, and much welcomed. A question: how appropriate or inappropriate would it be to draw an explicit one-to-one parallel between the economic cycle and the rhetorical cycle? Clearly, your work made a strong case for connections between the two -- but I'm wondering Resnick and Wolff's thoughts on production and distribution as a class cycle (and their accompanying constructions of exploitation happening in two different places; as appropriation at the point of production and as appropriation at the point of distribution) as directly parallel to invention and delivery (perhaps as a class cycle as well?). Makes me wish I hadn't missed the CW sessions explicitly focused on the canon of delivery. Any thoughts?
